correctness.rationale: For \(n=p^{\ell}m\), prime \(\ell\) gives exactly two exponent divisors at \(p\), while squarefree \(m\) contributes one at each other prime. Direct substitution gives \(d_e(n)=2\), \(\sigma_e(n)=mp(1+p^{\ell-1})\), and \(S_e(n)=1+p^{\ell-1}\). Type 1 would force \(1+p^{\ell-1}\mid2\), which is impossible. Type 2 is exactly \(1+p^{\ell-1}\mid2m\). Dividing the single possible factor \(2\) yields the stated \(M\)-criterion. A separate exact-integer checker recomputes the original definitions on 47,460 triples without discrepancy.

value.rationale: Prime exponents are the first nontrivial exponent-divisor layer because they have exactly two positive exponent divisors. The theorem therefore resolves a natural complete stratum rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. It exposes a sharp qualitative split between types 1 and 2 and reduces type-2 membership to the squarefree support of a single explicit integer \(M\); the two-prime-support corollary becomes one primality condition.
